mainTopic: Replanted and pot-grown produce: tithes, טבל and תרומה, כלאים in a pot with no hole, and the new משנה of the five grains
overview: This amud finishes רבה's question about produce that was tithed, then replanted, and then grew more. Does it follow the original, already-tithed part or the new growth? אביי asks how this differs from ordinary wheat and barley. רבה explains that he is asking only about a plant whose seed does not rot away. A proof from a tithed ליטרא of onions is rejected, because planting whole onions is their normal way of being sown. A question about a pot with no hole that later gets a hole is shown to be one sowing, unlike רבה's case of two sowings. רבי אבהו asks whether grain that became טבל and was replanted can be made תרומה while still growing. אביי defends the view that it can, explaining that the teaching 'there is no תרומה attached to the ground' is only about death and the extra fifth, since eating attached produce is not normal eating. Then אביי asks what שמואל's ban on planting כלאים in a pot with no hole adds, since a משנה in דמאי already teaches this. A new משנה lists the five grains for חלה, חדש and the עומר, and the גמרא begins sorting them into the wheat and barley families.

steps.title: Finishing the question: tithed produce that was replanted and grew more
steps.stepSummary: The case of רבה's question is finished: produce was estimated, tithed, replanted, and then it grew more.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he estimated the produce, separated מעשר from it, planted it, and it grew more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the case of רבה's question, which began just before this line. Someone tithed his produce, planted it again, and it grew bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the question is that some of this produce has already had מעשר taken from it, but now there is new growth on top. Do we say the plant keeps its 'already tithed' status because of the original part, or does the new growth make it need מעשר again?

keyTerms.meaning: He estimated them (how much מעשר is needed)
He separated מעשר from them
He planted them
It added (grew more)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new topic. It is the end of רבה's question, which started before this passage. Read it as the details of that same case.

phrases.english: where he estimated them and tithed them,
and planted them, and they grew more.
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The word in square brackets is the corrected wording, and it means the same thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the case of רבה's question, which began before this passage.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does tithed produce that was replanted and grew more follow its original, already-tithed part, or its new growth?

steps.title: Second question: if the new growth needs מעשר, what about the original part?
steps.stepSummary: רבה asks a second question: even if the new growth must be tithed, does the original part need to be tithed again?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you decide that we do not follow the original part, so the added growth needs מעשר, what about the original part?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה asks a second question that builds on the first. Suppose the new growth needs מעשר. Does the original part also need מעשר again?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The formula 'אם תמצא לומר' means: assume the first question is decided one way, and here is a further question. Even if the added growth is not covered by the old מעשר, the original part was already tithed once. So maybe it is exempt, or maybe it now counts as part of a new crop.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say (if the first question is decided this way)
We go after (we follow)
The original part (what was planted)
The added growth

phrases.english: If you will say,
we do not follow the original part,
and the added growth needs to be tithed,
what about the original part?
phrases.notes: He means: does the part that was already tithed need מעשר a second time?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a second question on top of the first one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If the added growth needs מעשר, does the original, already-tithed part also need מעשר again?

steps.title: אביי asks: how is this different from any wheat or barley?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: this looks like any ordinary grain that is tithed and then planted again.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: How is this different from all ordinary wheat and barley?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי questions whether רבה's question is a real question at all. People tithe wheat and barley and then plant them again all the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With ordinary grain, everyone agrees that the new crop needs its own מעשר. The old מעשר does not cover it. So אביי asks why רבה thinks his case could be any different.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Of the world (ordinary, everyday)
Wheat and barley

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
How is it different from all wheat
and barley in general?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מִכׇּל חִיטֵּי וּשְׂעָרֵי דְּעָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether רבה's question is a real question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's question about tithed produce that was replanted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ordinary wheat and barley are tithed and replanted all the time, and the new crop clearly needs its own מעשר. So there seems to be nothing to ask.

steps.title: רבה: my question is only about a seed that does not rot away
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that grain whose seed rots in the ground is obvious. He is asking only about a plant whose seed stays whole.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A thing whose seed disappears, I have no question about. My question is about a thing whose seed does not disappear. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי by narrowing his question. Wheat and barley seeds rot away in the ground, so that case is simple. He is asking about plants whose original seed stays in the ground and keeps growing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the seed rots away, the whole crop is new, so of course it needs new מעשר. When the original piece is still there and just gets bigger, you could say it is the same tithed item with something added. That is why רבה thinks his question is real.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant whose seed rots away in the ground
A plant whose seed does not rot away
I have no question about it

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's question is only about plants whose original seed stays whole in the ground. When the seed rots away, as with wheat and barley, the new crop clearly needs new מעשר.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ כָּלֶה – לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי,
phrases.english: A thing whose seed disappears, I have no question about,
phrases.notes: Like wheat and barley, where the seed rots in the ground and the whole crop is new.

phrases.english: rather, where I have my question is
a thing whose seed does not disappear. What is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר שֶׁזַּרְעוֹ כָּלֶה לָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought רבה was asking about ordinary grain like wheat and barley.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is only about a plant whose original seed stays in the ground and grows bigger.

steps.title: Trying to answer from רבי יוחנן's ruling on a ליטרא of onions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to answer רבה's question from a ruling that a tithed ליטרא of onions that was planted is tithed on the whole crop.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him answer it from what רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A ליטרא of onions that someone tithed and then planted is tithed on all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that רבה's question already has an answer. An onion's base stays in the ground and grows, so it is exactly the kind of plant רבה asked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן says the whole crop is tithed, including the original onions that were already tithed. That seems to answer both of רבה's questions. The new growth needs מעשר, and even the original part needs מעשר again.

keyTerms.meaning: Answer it (settle the question)
A ליטרא, a measure of weight
That he 'fixed' it, meaning he separated its מעשר
It is tithed on the whole amount

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof holds, the original part counts as new produce once it grows more. The earlier מעשר does not protect it.

phrases.english: Let him answer it from this,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: that רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
a ליטרא of onions that he tithed and then planted
is tithed according to all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּפְשׁוֹט לֵיהּ מֵהָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the narrowed question from an outside ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's question about a plant whose seed does not rot away, which was tithed and then grew more
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי יצחק in the name of רבי יוחנן: a tithed ליטרא of onions that was planted is tithed on the whole crop

steps.title: The onion case is different because that is how onions are normally sown
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the onions. Replanting whole onions is the normal way to sow onions, but replanting in רבה's case is not a normal sowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, with the onions, that is the normal way they are planted. Here, in רבה's case, that is not the normal way it is planted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the tithed ליטרא of onions. It says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Onions are normally planted whole, so the whole field counts as a fresh new crop and is tithed in full. In רבה's case the produce is planted in a way that is not the normal way to sow it. So the earlier growth may still count as already tithed, and the onion ruling cannot answer רבה's question.

keyTerms.meaning: sowing; planting
this is its normal way of being sown
there (the case being cited) / here (our case)

steps.whatToRemember: The onion proof fails. Whole onions are normally planted that way, but רבה's case is not a normal sowing, so his question stays open.

phrases.english: There, that is its normal sowing,
phrases.notes: "There" means the onion case from the proof. People normally plant whole onions.

phrases.english: here, that is not its normal sowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם – הַיְינוּ זְרִיעָתוֹ, הָכָא – לָאו הַיְינוּ זְרִיעָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 5
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the tithed onions that were replanted
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Onions are normally sown whole, so their case is a true new sowing. רבה's case is not a normal sowing, so the cases cannot be compared.

steps.title: A question about a pot without a hole
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בר מניומי asks אביי what the law is for a plant growing in a pot that has no hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בר מניומי said to אביי: what is the law for a pot that has no hole?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked, about a plant in a pot with no hole in it. This sets up אביי's response in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plant in a pot without a hole is not connected to the ground. This affects how it must be tithed. The question is short, and as written it is unclear what exactly is being asked.

keyTerms.meaning: a flowerpot or planter
perforated; having a hole in the bottom
what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina bar Minyumi said to Abaye:
A flowerpot that is not perforated, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new, related question after רבה's question has been discussed
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How tithing works for produce grown in a pot with no hole

steps.title: אביי says a pot with no hole is simply a pot with no hole
steps.stepSummary: אביי responds that if the pot has no hole, the law is just the known law of a pot with no hole, so there is nothing to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it has no hole, then it is just a pot with no hole!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the question seems pointless. A pot with no hole already has a known law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law for a pot with no hole is already set, so asking about it plainly makes no sense. This pushes אביי to look for a deeper meaning in the question, which he does in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: if
then it is; this is

phrases.english: If it is not perforated,
phrases.notes: אביי is the one speaking here.

phrases.english: then it is a non-perforated pot!
phrases.notes: He means it simply follows the known rule for a pot without a hole.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לֹא נָקוּב – הָא לֹא נָקוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question of step 7 by saying its plain meaning is obvious
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A pot with no hole follows the regular, known law for such a pot.

steps.title: Maybe you mean the pot was later given a hole
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests the real question: the plant grew in a pot with no hole, and then a hole was made in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps you are asking about a case where he later went and made a hole in it?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי guesses what רבי חנינא really meant. The case is a plant that grew first without a hole, and then a hole was made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the plant has two stages of growth: one while cut off from the ground and one while connected to it. The question becomes whether the earlier growth joins the later growth and is treated the same way. This is very similar to רבה's question about earlier growth and new growth.

keyTerms.meaning: perhaps
he went back and made a hole in it
are you saying?

steps.confusionAlert: Both questions ask the same thing: does earlier growth get treated like the later growth? Do not mix them up, though. In רבה's case the produce was taken out and planted again. Here the plant never left the pot.

phrases.english: Perhaps you are saying that he went back and perforated it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Redefines the question of step 7 so that it becomes a real question
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether growth from before the hole was made is treated together with growth from after it

steps.title: The pot is one sowing, but רבה's case is two sowings
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the pot case is a single sowing that simply becomes attached to the ground, while רבה's case has two separate sowings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it is one sowing; it just becomes attached and grows. There, in רבה's case, there are two sowings.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows that the pot question is not the same as רבה's question. In the pot there was only one planting, so the whole plant is treated as one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the hole is made, the plant becomes connected to the ground and keeps growing from that same planting. So the whole plant is treated as growing from the ground. In רבה's case the produce was planted twice, so it is a real question whether the second planting joins the first.

keyTerms.meaning: one single sowing
it simply becomes attached (to the ground)
rises; grows upward
two separate sowings

steps.whatToRemember: A pot that later gets a hole is one planting that becomes attached to the ground. רבה's replanted produce is two plantings, so his question remains a real question.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the main idea behind רבה's question: the doubt only comes up when there are two separate plantings.

phrases.english: Here, it is one sowing;
phrases.notes: "Here" is the pot that was later given a hole.

phrases.english: it is just becoming attached and rising;
there, they are two sowings.
phrases.notes: "There" is רבה's case, where the produce was taken out and planted again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clarified question of step 9 by separating it from רבה's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pot case is one sowing that becomes attached to the ground, so the whole plant is treated as one. רבה's case has two sowings, so it is different.

steps.title: Grain made טבל, replanted, then designated while growing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו asks whether grain that became טבל through smoothing, and was then replanted, can be made תרומה while attached to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו asked: An ear of grain was smoothed in a pile, then planted again, and then someone called it תרומה while it was still growing. What is the law? Since smoothing made it טבל, maybe calling it תרומה works. Or maybe, once it was planted again, its טבל status was cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו opens a new question. He wants to know if replanting erases the טבל status that the grain already had.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Smoothing the pile (מירוח) is the step that makes grain obligated in תרומה and מעשר, so the grain is now טבל. The question is whether that status survives once the grain goes back into the ground. If it survives, calling it תרומה works even while it grows. If replanting cancels it, the designation does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: He asks a question that may not have a clear answer
Smoothing the grain pile, the step that makes produce obligated in תרומה and מעשר
A pile of grain
Produce that is obligated in תרומה and מעשר but has not had them taken yet
He designated it, calling it תרומה or מעשר
Lapsed, was cancelled

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the earlier case of רבה. Here the grain was already smoothed into a pile, so it had become טבל, before it was planted again.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu asked:
An ear of grain that one smoothed into a pile,
phrases.notes: Smoothing the pile is the step that makes grain obligated in תרומה and מעשר.

phrases.english: and then he planted it again,
and he designated it while it was attached to the ground: what is the law?
Do we say: since he smoothed it, he made it טבל,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָרָא עָלֶיהָ שֵׁם קָדְשָׁה לַהּ,
phrases.english: so when he designated it, he made it holy?
Or perhaps, since he planted it again,
its טבל status was cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about replanting, similar in theme to the earlier replanting discussion with רבה and the pot case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does replanting cancel the טבל status created by smoothing, so that designating the grain as תרומה while it is attached does not work?

steps.title: That would mean תרומה attached to the ground
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge אביי: if the designation works, we would have תרומה attached to the ground, but a teaching says this never happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to אביי: If so, we would find תרומה attached to the ground. But we learned: we never find תרומה attached to the ground!
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן challenge אביי, who apparently answered רבי אבהו's question by saying the designation works. They quote a teaching that seems to rule it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If calling the growing grain תרומה works, then real תרומה would be growing in the field. But a known teaching says there is no such thing as תרומה attached to the ground. So it seems replanting must cancel the טבל status.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן, which is holy
If so, if that were true
We do not find, there is no such case
Attached to the ground, still growing

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָצִינוּ תְּרוּמָה בִּמְחוּבָּר לַקַּרְקַע,
phrases.english: If so, we have found תרומה attached to the ground,

phrases.aramaic: וּתְנַן: לֹא מָצִינוּ תְּרוּמָה בִּמְחוּבָּר לַקַּרְקַע!
phrases.english: but we learned: We do not find תרומה attached to the ground!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, מָצִינוּ תְּרוּמָה בִּמְחוּבָּר לַקַּרְקַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first side of רבי אבהו's question.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that designating the replanted grain as תרומה takes effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching says תרומה is never found attached to the ground, so the designation cannot work.

steps.title: The teaching is only about death and the extra fifth
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the teaching only means no one gets the punishment of death or the extra fifth for eating attached תרומה, because eating it attached is not normal eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That teaching is about being liable to death or the extra fifth. If he picks it and eats it, it is already detached. If he bends down and eats it from the ground, his way of eating is so unusual that it does not count.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by narrowing what the teaching means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching does not say תרומה can never exist on attached produce. It only says there is never a punishment for eating attached תרומה. Once it is picked it is detached, and eating it straight from the ground is so odd that normal people would not call it eating. So the designation can still work.

keyTerms.meaning: Death by the hand of Heaven, the punishment for a non-כהן who eats תרומה on purpose
The extra fifth paid by a non-כהן who ate תרומה by mistake
Detached from the ground
Bends down
His behavior is so unusual it does not count, since everyone else would not act that way

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common idea: an unusual way of doing something often does not count legally, even when the status itself, here תרומה, is real.

phrases.english: He said to him: When that teaching was taught,
it was about being liable to death or the extra fifth,
because if he picks it and eats it, it is already detached,
and if he bends down and eats it from the ground,
his way of acting does not count, compared to how all people act.
phrases.notes: Nobody normally eats grain straight off the stalk in the field, so it is not called eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of the רבנן by limiting the teaching they quoted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the quoted teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The teaching meant תרומה can never exist while attached to the ground.
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching only means there is no death penalty or extra fifth for attached תרומה, since eating it attached is not normal eating.

steps.title: But unusual eating of eggs inside a bird does count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges אביי from the tablet of אילפא, where eggs eaten from inside a dead kosher bird do count as eating, even though that is unusual.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from what was written on אילפא's tablet: eggs of a dead kosher bird, some outside the bird and some inside. The ones eaten from inside make the eater's clothes טמא while in his throat. The ones from outside do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer. Its reply comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said unusual eating does not count. But eating eggs from inside a bird's carcass is also unusual, yet it counts as eating the נבלה and makes the clothes טמא. So why should bending down to eat attached תרומה not count too?

keyTerms.meaning: And how is this different? A challenge comparing two cases
A writing tablet or notebook
The carcass of a kosher bird that was not properly slaughtered
Make clothes טמא
The throat, while the food is being swallowed

phrases.english: And how is this different from what is written
on the tablet of Ilfa:
Eggs of the carcass of a kosher bird,
some of them outside the bird and some inside:
eaten from inside, they make clothes impure while in the throat,
phrases.notes: Eating a dead kosher bird makes the eater's clothes טמא while it is going down his throat.

phrases.aramaic: מִבַּחוּץ אֵין מְטַמְּאִין בְּגָדִים אַבֵּית הַבְּלִיעָה.
phrases.english: from outside, they do not make clothes impure while in the throat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer that unusual eating does not count.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that eating attached תרומה by bending down does not count because it is unusual.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating eggs from inside a bird's carcass is also unusual, yet it counts as eating for טומאה. So unusual eating should count for תרומה as well.

steps.title: Detached food is sometimes eaten that way, attached food never is
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the eggs: people do sometimes eat detached food in odd ways, but nobody eats produce while it is still attached to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: With something detached, people do sometimes eat it this way. With something attached to the ground, people do not eat it like that at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends אביי against the challenge from the eggs in the dead bird. It draws a line between detached food and attached food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eggs are already detached from anything, so eating them is unusual but still something people do. Eating grain while it is attached to the ground is not done at all. So אביי's point stands: eating attached תרומה is not counted as eating, and there is no death penalty or extra fifth for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Detached, not connected to the ground or its source
Attached to the ground
People commonly do this

steps.whatToRemember: Unusual eating still counts if people sometimes eat that way (the eggs). Eating something attached to the ground is not normal eating at all, so it is not treated as eating.

phrases.english: With something detached, people do commonly
phrases.notes: He means the eggs inside the bird from the tablet of אילפא.

phrases.english: eat it this way,
but with something attached, people do not commonly eat it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by telling apart the eggs case from attached produce.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since unusual eating of eggs counts, unusual eating of attached תרומה should also count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Detached food eaten oddly is still a way people eat. Attached food is never eaten that way, so it does not count as eating.

steps.title: Planting mixed seeds in a pot with no hole is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב טביומי בר קיסנא quotes שמואל: if someone plants כלאים in a pot that has no hole, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טביומי בר קיסנא said in the name of שמואל: Someone who plants mixed kinds in a pot with no hole is doing something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. שמואל rules that planting כלאים in a pot with no hole is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pot with no hole is not connected to the ground, so by Torah law planting in it is not real planting. Still, שמואל says planting mixed kinds there is forbidden. This links to the earlier talk about pots and planting in the sugya.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden mixtures, here planting different kinds of seeds together
A flowerpot with no hole, so it is not connected to the ground
One who plants or sows

phrases.english: Rav Tavyumei bar Kisna said,
Shmuel said:
One who plants diverse kinds
in a pot with no hole: it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טָבְיוֹמֵי בַּר קִיסְנָא אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement, related in theme to the earlier pot cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Planting כלאים in a pot with no hole is forbidden.

steps.title: What new thing is שמואל teaching
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks what שמואל's ruling adds. If he had said the planter gets rabbinic lashes, that would be new, but just saying 'forbidden' only tells us it counts as planting by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: If שמואל had taught that the person gets lashes for rebelliousness by rabbinic law, that would make sense. But when he just says 'forbidden', what is he teaching us? That by rabbinic law this counts as planting?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges שמואל's ruling by asking what is new in it. This step sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ruling of 'forbidden' only teaches that planting in a pot with no hole counts as planting by rabbinic law. אביי is about to show that this was already known. If שמואל had spoken about lashes, that would have added a real new point.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes for rebelliousness, a rabbinic punishment
By rabbinic law
It would be fine if, used to set up a challenge
What is he teaching us? (what is new here)
Sowing, planting

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It would be fine if he had taught us that
he is given lashes for rebelliousness by rabbinic law; that would be well,
but saying 'forbidden',
what is he teaching us?
That by rabbinic law it counts as sowing?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא אִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן לוֹקֶה מַכַּת מַרְדּוּת מִדְּרַבָּנַן שַׁפִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 16 as adding nothing new.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that planting כלאים in a pot with no hole is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only point of the ruling is that it counts as planting by rabbinic law, and that point is already known, so the ruling adds nothing.

steps.title: We already learned this from the משנה in דמאי
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows from a משנה that growing in a pot with no hole already counts by rabbinic law: תרומה taken from such produce is תרומה, but one must separate again.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned: If someone separated תרומה from produce of a pot with no hole for produce of a pot with a hole, it is תרומה, but he must separate תרומה again.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings the source that proves his point: a משנה already teaches that growing in a pot with no hole counts by rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce from a pot with no hole owes תרומה only by rabbinic law, while produce from a pot with a hole owes it by Torah law. Since the separation still counts as תרומה, growing in the pot with no hole must count as growing by rabbinic law. So שמואל's 'forbidden' seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: He separated תרומה
A pot with a hole, treated like the ground
And he must separate תרומה again

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the separation is useless. It IS תרומה (by rabbinic law), but it is not enough for the Torah-level produce, so he must separate again.

phrases.english: We already learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in דמאי.

phrases.english: If he separated teruma from produce of a pot with no hole for produce of a pot with a hole,
it is teruma, and he must separate teruma again.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's challenge by bringing the source showing שמואל's point is already known.
steps.raayaObject: That planting in a pot with no hole counts as planting by rabbinic law, which makes שמואל's ruling seem unneeded
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in דמאי: תרומה from a pot with no hole for a pot with a hole is תרומה, but one must separate again

steps.title: The five grains owe חלה and combine together
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists the five grains: wheat, barley, spelt, oats and rye. They are obligated in חלה and join together to make up the needed amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Wheat, barley, spelt, oats and rye are obligated in חלה, and they combine with each other.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the five grains and says they owe חלה and combine with each other for the amount of dough that requires חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only these five grains count for חלה. Dough made from a mix of them can be added together to reach the amount that requires taking חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of dough given to a כהן
They combine to make up the needed amount
Spelt
Oats
Rye

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Wheat, barley, spelt,
oats, and rye:
these are obligated in challa,
and they combine with one another,
phrases.notes: He means they add up together to reach the amount of dough that owes חלה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, a fresh topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five grains are obligated in חלה and combine with each other.

steps.title: The five grains and the laws of חדש and the עומר
steps.stepSummary: The same five grains are forbidden as חדש before פסח and may not be cut before the עומר. If they took root before the עומר, the עומר permits them; if not, they wait for next year's עומר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are forbidden as new grain before פסח, and may not be cut before the עומר. If they took root before the עומר, the עומר permits them. If not, they are forbidden until the next עומר comes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues. It teaches that these five grains fall under the law of חדש and the rules about cutting before the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New grain may not be eaten until the עומר is brought, and it may not be cut before then either. What decides which עומר permits the grain is when it took root: before this year's עומר, or only after it.

keyTerms.meaning: New grain, forbidden until the עומר is brought
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
They took root
From cutting the harvest

steps.whatToRemember: The five grains: they owe חלה, combine together, and are under חדש. Taking root before the עומר is what lets this year's עומר permit them.

phrases.english: and they are forbidden as new grain before Passover,
and forbidden to be cut before the omer.
If they took root before the omer,
the omer permits them,
and if not, they are forbidden
until the next omer comes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with more laws about the five grains.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The five grains are forbidden as חדש before the עומר and may not be cut before it; taking root before the עומר lets that עומר permit them, otherwise they wait for the next one.

steps.title: Spelt is a kind of wheat; oats and rye are kinds of barley
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא sorts the three less-familiar grains of the משנה: כוסמין belongs to the wheat family, and שיבולת שועל and שיפון belong to the barley family.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A ברייתא taught: Spelt is a type of wheat. Oats and rye are types of barley.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by quoting a ברייתא that groups the five grains into two families.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed five grains, but it did not say how they relate to each other. The ברייתא adds that there are really only two basic families: wheat (wheat and spelt) and barley (barley, oats and rye). This grouping matters for laws that depend on whether two grains count as the same kind.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
Spelt, a grain in the wheat family
Oats (literally 'fox's ear of grain'), a grain in the barley family
Rye, a grain in the barley family
A type of wheat
A type of barley

steps.whatToRemember: Five grains, two families: wheat + spelt, and barley + oats + rye.
steps.whyThisMatters: Knowing which grains are the same kind helps when a law depends on grains being similar, such as grains combining with each other.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was taught in a ברייתא:
Spelt is a type of wheat,
oats and rye are a type of barley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה of the five grains (steps 19-20) by defining how the grains are related.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כוסמין is in the wheat family; שיבולת שועל and שיפון are in the barley family.

steps.title: Starting to give the everyday name of spelt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins giving the common Aramaic names of the less familiar grains, starting with כוסמין. The name itself comes right after this.
steps.simpleTranslation: Spelt is called...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it is about to tell us what כוסמין is called in everyday language. The answer continues in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After grouping the grains into families, the גמרא now switches to identifying them by their common names, so the learner knows exactly which plants the משנה means. Only the opening word appears here; the actual name follows.

phrases.english: Spelt is called —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from grouping the grains into families to naming each grain in everyday language.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the common-language name of כוסמין (completed in the following text).
